📖 User Guide — How to Run the Books

Everything you need in one place: where to begin, the daily routine, what each page does, and how to fix mistakes. Tap a heading to open it.

✅ Setup checklist

1. Where should posting begin?

Start on the first day of a month, with opening balances for that date. Pick one of two routes:

  • Complete records for this year: start on 1 January (or your financial-year start). Reports then cover the whole year, but you have to catch up every month so far.
  • Patchy or missing records: start on the 1st of the current month and enter the closing balances of the month before as your opening balances. This is quicker and cleaner. Older months can be added later from Historical Years.

How opening balances work in this system (Opening Balances):

  • Enter assets (Cash 1010, Bank 1020, M-Pesa 1030, etc.) as Debit.
  • Enter liabilities (loans, unpaid bills) as Credit.
  • Enter the balance of each special fund (Building, Youth, Missions…) as Credit on its fund account (3020, 3040, 3070…).
  • Whatever is left automatically becomes the General Fund (3010) — you don't enter it yourself.
  • The system always dates opening balances 1 January of the year you choose, even if you start mid-year. That is fine: the balance sheet will be right, but income and expense reports will only cover the months you actually post.
  • Count the cash and check the bank and M-Pesa statements before entering figures, so they are real.
Land, buildings and equipment you already own should go in as opening balances. Do not post them through Capital Expenditure — that would reduce your cash again. Note: assets entered as opening balances do not appear in the Asset Register or Depreciation schedule; only new purchases made through Capital Expenditure do.
2. Your routine — daily, weekly, monthly, yearly
WhenWhat to doWhere
After each serviceRecord each member's tithe, then the offerings, special contributions and any other income.Tithes · Offerings
As money is spentRecord bills paid, salaries and ministry costs. Small cash payments go to Petty Cash.Expenses · Petty Cash
When it happensNew purchases of land, equipment, furniture etc.; money moved between funds; anything unusual (bank charges, loans, interest).Capital Expenditure · Fund Transfer · Daily Posting
End of every monthCompare the ledger's Cash, Bank and M-Pesa balances with your actual cash count and the bank and M-Pesa statements. Fix any difference. Then take a snapshot and back up.General Ledger · Backup
End of yearPost depreciation, review the financial statements, then carry balances forward to the new year.Depreciation · Reports · Historical Years

4. Tithes vs Offerings, and one-posting-does-it-all
  • Tithes are personal — always name the member. Offerings are usually congregational — leave the giver blank unless someone gave a named special gift.
  • After you save an entry, the date, fund, payment method and service stay filled in so you can enter a whole Sunday quickly. Tick Show receipt after saving if you want a receipt each time.
  • In Daily Posting, choose the debit and credit accounts. Extra fields appear when needed (contributor for income, payee for expenses, asset details for purchases). One posting then appears in the ledger and the right register.
  • The Posting Calendar shows each day's postings (green = income, red = expense, badge = number of entries). Click a day to set the posting date and see that day's entries.
5. Fixing mistakes — Amend, Repost, Void, Delete, Restore
SituationUse
Wrong amount, account, date or name — and you want a visible trail✏️ Amend → With audit trail. The original is reversed and a correcting entry is posted. Best choice after the month has been reconciled.
A simple typing slip you caught right away✏️ Amend → Edit in place. Quick fix, no reversal entries; the change is still logged in the Audit Log.
The entry needs several things changed🔁 Repost. It loads the entry into Daily Posting pre-filled; you correct it and post, and the original is voided (or deleted) automatically.
The entry should never have been made🚫 Void (keeps a reversal trail) or 🗑 Delete (moves it to the Deleted Bin).
You voided or deleted the wrong one↩ Restore from the "Voided / amended" or "Deleted bin" view on the Amendments page.
  • Find the ✏️ Fix button on the Tithes, Offerings, Expenses and Posting Calendar lists, or use the full list on the Amendments page.
  • Every action asks for a reason, and everything appears in the Audit Log.
  • Multi-line journals can be voided or deleted as a whole, but to change one you void/delete it and re-enter it.
  • Rule of thumb: before a month is reconciled, Edit in place or Delete is fine. After it, use Amend with audit trail or Void.
6. Month-end checklist
  1. Make sure every tithe, offering and expense for the month has been entered.
  2. Count the cash in hand. Compare it with the ledger's 1010 Cash balance.
  3. Compare the bank statement with 1020 Bank, and the M-Pesa statement with 1030 M-Pesa.
  4. If a balance is off, look for a missing, duplicated or mis-dated entry using the Posting Calendar and General Ledger, and correct it with Amend or Repost.
  5. Check Petty Cash against the float.
  6. Review the Dashboard and Financial Statements.
  7. Take a snapshot and download a backup from Backup / Restore.
7. Do's and don'ts
✔ Do
  • Change the default password before real data goes in.
  • Download a backup after every session.
  • Use one receipt/reference per entry and keep paper receipts filed by number.
  • Post on the date the money actually moved.
  • Record fund-specific gifts against the right fund.
✘ Don't
  • Don't post assets you already own through Capital Expenditure.
  • Don't use Delete on reconciled months — Amend or Void instead.
  • Don't clear your browser data or use private/incognito windows without a backup.
  • Don't enter the same offering twice (once on the Offerings page and again in Daily Posting).
  • Don't share the password with people who shouldn't see the finances.
8. Safety, backups and troubleshooting
  • Your data is stored in this browser on this device. If the browser data is cleared, or you open the file on another computer, it will look empty. A backup file is your only protection — keep copies on a flash disk or email them to yourself.
  • To move to another device: Backup on the old one, then Restore on the new one.
  • Your password is stored only in this browser and cannot be recovered if you forget it — write it down and keep backups. Change password · Edit church name & address.
  • If a page looks stale, press Refresh on the Dashboard or reload the page — your data is not lost.
  • Importing old records from Excel/CSV: use Upload Data (download the template first) or Historical Years for earlier years.
9. Training mode, daily collection, back-dating, reconciliation, I&E
  • Training mode (button in the top bar): a separate set of practice books with sample data. Real books are never touched. Use Reset training data to start over, Back to real books to leave. A sample wrong entry is planted — practise fixing it.
  • Daily Collection: enter the whole day's tithes, offerings and special gifts on one sheet; it distributes to the registers, member history and ledger in one go. Made a mistake in the sheet? Correct batch reloads it for editing and voids the old lines.
  • Back-dating: choose the real date on any posting screen. The checker lists Sundays with nothing posted so you can fill the gaps.
  • Bank Reconciliation: tick what is on the statement, add bank charges/interest, aim for a difference of 0.00, then save. Do it monthly for Bank and M-Pesa and count Cash.
  • Income & Expenditure Account: any date range, by fund, by month or compared with last year; print or export to Excel.
  • Wrong entry? Amendments → Scan all entries finds suspicious items; Fix & redirect moves the amount to the right account with a reversal trail.

✏️ Transaction Amendments & Corrections

Made a mistake? ✏️ Amend fixes an entry (with a reversal trail, or quietly in place) · 🔁 Repost loads it into Daily Posting so you can correct it and post again · 🚫 Void cancels it with a reversal · 🗑 Delete removes it to a bin you can restore from. Every action is recorded in the Audit Log.

🛠 Error check — find entries that look wrong

Looks for duplicates, accounts missing from the chart, income/expense posted the wrong way round, tithes with no member, future dates and unusually large amounts. Press Fix & redirect to move the amount to the correct account — the original is kept with a reversal trail.

🏢 National Head Office — Finance & Consolidation

A standalone National Head Office accounting workspace. Its transactions, schedules and statements are stored separately from the ordinary church ledger and Regional AGM Reports.

Separate records: entries posted here stay in the National Head Office register and are used only by the Head Office statement pack. They are not posted to the main ledger. Regional AGM Reports keeps its own independent data and reporting workflow.

🧾 National Head Office — Accounting Integrity Review

Check Head Office journals, opening balances, fund controls, bank reconciliation, fixed assets and supporting schedules before approving statements.

Tap “Run Accounting Review” to generate the control checklist.

🎓 Training Guide — How to Enter National Head Office Data

Use this guide to practise entering records in the separate National Head Office books. Follow the steps in order; use realistic sample figures while learning.

Step 1 — Set up the financial year and Head Office details

Check the financial year and complete the relevant Head Office details before entering transactions. Save the details when a Save button is provided.

Step 2 — Enter income and expenditure
  1. Open National Head Office Transaction Entry.
  2. Choose the transaction date and the correct income or expense category.
  3. Enter the description/reference and amount in KSh.
  4. Check the debit/credit or account fields carefully, then save the entry.
  5. Confirm that the entry appears in the Head Office register. Correct mistakes using the available edit/amendment controls.
Step 3 — Add centers and center accounts

In Centers Network — Separate Center Accounts, add each center using the official name entered by the administrator. Enter that center's transactions and opening balances only in its own account. Do not mix center figures into Head Office transactions.

Step 4 — Enter budgets and estimates

Open the Head Office budget section, choose the financial year, add each budget line and its approved/proposed amount, and save. Use clear descriptions and enter each line once. The Budget vs Actual report compares saved budgets with matching actual entries; Budget Estimates shows the proposed plan.

Step 5 — Enter the 15% church contribution schedule

Add a region, then enter each church/branch and its contribution amount. Check regional subtotals and the grand total against the source schedule before printing.

Step 6 — Review statements and print

Open the Final Statement Pack and view the Income Statement, Balance Sheet, Budget vs Actual, Budget Estimates, or an individual center statement. Check the year, names, amounts and totals before using the report's own Print / Save as PDF button.

Training tip: Start with a small test entry, verify it in the register and statement, then practise editing or removing it if needed. National Head Office and Regional AGM records are separate. In Training Mode, confirm the 🎓 TRAINING banner is visible before practising; never use sample figures as official accounts.

🎓 Training Guide — How to Enter Regional AGM Data

Use this guide to prepare a Regional AGM report pack. The regional records are independent of National Head Office and the main church ledger.

Step 1 — Set the region and financial year

At the top of Regional AGM Reports, enter the correct financial year and region name, then tap Save details. Check these before entering figures.

Step 2 — Enter church contributions

Open the church contribution schedule. Add each church using its correct name and enter the amount received for the selected year. Confirm the displayed total against your source records.

Step 3 — Enter income and expenditure
  1. Open the relevant Regional AGM income/expenditure entry area.
  2. Choose the date and appropriate category/account.
  3. Enter a clear description/reference and amount in KSh.
  4. Save, then verify the entry appears in the relevant table and affects the expected total.
Step 4 — Enter remittances and balances

Record remittances and outstanding balances using the correct church and period. Distinguish amounts received from amounts still owing; check that totals reconcile to supporting records.

Step 5 — Add the proposed budget and estimates

Enter each planned income and expenditure line for the upcoming period. Use clear budget descriptions, check the proposed totals and projected surplus/deficit, and avoid entering actual transactions as estimates.

Step 6 — Review statements and produce AGM reports

Review the Income & Expenditure Statement, Balance Sheet, contribution/remittance schedules and budget reports. Correct errors before printing the AGM pack or creating a Regional AGM PowerPoint presentation.

Training tip: Enter one sample church and a few sample figures first, save them, and check the resulting report. Confirm the 🎓 TRAINING banner is visible when practising in Training Mode. Do not present practice data as official AGM figures.
